title: Budget back in surplus in August after two months in red | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 05:56
-     - 278

President and Finance Minister Anura Kumara Dissanayake

The Government’s Budget returned to surplus in August, posting a cumulative surplus of Rs. 35.4 billion for the first eight months of 2026, after deficits in June and July had pushed the balance into the red, the Finance Ministry’s latest Fiscal Review Report showed.

The turnaround implies a surplus of around Rs. 145 billion for August alone, against a cumulative deficit of Rs. 109.72 billion at end-July. Monthly revenue rose and expenditure fell in August from the levels of June and July.

The August surplus follows deficits of around Rs. 188 billion in June and Rs. 119 billion in July, which had wiped out a cumulative surplus of Rs. 197 billion at end-May.

The Ministry’s data show a surplus of a similar size in August 2025.

The eight-month surplus compares with a deficit of Rs. 411 billion in the same period of 2025.

Total revenue and grants rose 21.2% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs. 4,002.3 billion from Rs. 3,301.5 billion, while total expenditure rose a slower 6.9% YoY to Rs. 3,966.9 billion from Rs. 3,712.5 billion. The Ministry attributed the improvement mainly to revenue growth, along with what it described as the rationalisation of Government expenditure.

The primary balance, which excludes interest payments and is a key indicator under Sri Lanka’s International Monetary Fund (IMF)-supported program, posted a surplus of Rs. 1,644.6 billion, up 28.8% YoY from Rs. 1,276.5 billion. This is more than four times the Rs. 360 billion primary surplus estimated for the full year in the 2026 Budget, which projects an annual overall deficit of Rs. 2,257 billion.

Tax revenue rose 20% YoY to Rs. 3,684 billion and non-tax revenue 39.1% to Rs. 315 billion, while grants fell 40.1% to Rs. 4 billion. Revenue excluding grants rose 21% to Rs. 3,998.3 billion, which the Ministry attributed mainly to collections from motor vehicles.

Revenue from Value Added Tax (VAT) rose 22% YoY to Rs. 1,322.7 billion from Rs. 1,084.2 billion, with VAT on imports up 16% to Rs. 599 billion and VAT on domestic activities up 28%. Income tax revenue rose 18% to Rs. 825.6 billion from Rs. 702.4 billion.

Excise duty collected by Sri Lanka Customs rose 23% YoY to Rs. 565.6 billion from Rs. 461.4 billion. Excise duty on motor vehicles, which made up 61% of that amount, increased by Rs. 76.5 billion to Rs. 347 billion. Excise duty on liquor collected by the Excise Department rose 24% to Rs. 181.1 billion from Rs. 145.7 billion.

Total revenue and grants reached 75.5% of the annual estimate of Rs. 5,300 billion by end-August, with tax revenue at 75% of its Rs. 4,910 billion target. Sri Lanka Customs achieved 78.3% of its annual estimate, the Excise Department 74.5%, and the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) 71.9%. Customs and the IRD each accounted for 47% of tax revenue.

On the spending side, recurrent expenditure rose 4.4% YoY to Rs. 3,531 billion from Rs. 3,381.3 billion. Interest payments, which made up 46% of recurrent spending, fell 4.6% to Rs. 1,609.2 billion from Rs. 1,687.6 billion.

Capital expenditure and net lending rose 31.6% YoY to Rs. 435.9 billion from Rs. 331.2 billion, but reached only 25.4% of the annual allocation of Rs. 1,719 billion, against 60.5% for recurrent expenditure. Total expenditure stood at 52.5% of the Rs. 7,557 billion annual estimate.

The IMF has urged the Government to accelerate public spending execution, including disaster-related support, and has said the Government remains committed to restoring the primary surplus target to 2.3% of GDP in 2027, following temporary fiscal easing this year.

The economy expanded by 4.2% YoY in the second quarter of 2026, slower than the 5% growth recorded a year earlier.

title: Banks build foreign buffer as private sector keeps cutting offshore debt | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 05:54
-     - 325

Sri Lanka’s banks have built up their foreign currency holdings abroad while cutting what they owe overseas, and private companies have continued to repay more foreign debt than they take on, the Central Bank of Sri Lanka’s (CBSL) External Sector Bulletin for August 2026 showed.

The banking sector’s foreign assets, which include deposits and placements with banks abroad and holdings of foreign securities, rose to $ 6.6 billion by end-July from $ 5.5 billion at end-2025.

Its foreign liabilities, which include foreign borrowings, credit lines, and deposits from non-residents, eased to $ 5 billion from $ 5.5 billion over the same period.

That left banks with net foreign assets of about $ 1.6 billion, the widest gap in the bulletin’s data series, which begins in 2015.

The position has reversed over the decade. In 2015, banks held $ 2 billion in foreign assets against $ 9.1 billion in foreign liabilities. Liabilities declined steadily thereafter, falling to $ 5.4 billion in 2022, while assets rose to $ 4 billion that year. Assets first overtook liabilities in 2023, at $ 5 billion against $ 4.9 billion.

Interest paid by deposit-taking institutions on foreign loans rose 13.3% to $ 40.3 million in January to August 2026, from $ 35.6 million a year earlier.

Net foreign borrowing by the private sector, the difference between new foreign loans and repayments of existing ones, was negative at $ 94 million in the first half of 2026. This means companies repaid more foreign debt than they raised. Net repayments were $ 183 million in 2025 and $ 575 million in 2024.

Repayments since the start of 2023 total about $ 1.1 billion. The private sector has been a net repayer of foreign loans every year since 2019, with the exception of 2022, when it recorded a marginal net inflow of $ 9 million. Net foreign borrowing peaked at $ 211 million in 2017.

Gross official reserves, including the swap facility with the People’s Bank of China (PBOC), stood at $ 6.9 billion at end-August 2026.

title: RTI action compels Royal College  to furnish info on alleged fiasco over rugby season ticket money lost | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 05:52
-     - 435

Royal College, Colombo

In a landmark verdict (Appeal No. RTIC/Appeal/556/2024), the Right to Information Commission (RTIC) has ordered Royal College, Colombo 7, to immediately hand over hidden accounting records detailing an alleged multi-million rupee fraud involving short-banked match ticket sales.

The ruling delivers a stinging rebuke to school authorities who insisted that their elite alumni body operated beyond the reach of State audit laws.

The controversy traces back to the First XV rugby seasons of 2017 and 2018 at the Royal College Sports Complex.

According to official RTI filings and surrounding litigation, ticket sale proceeds exceeding Rs. 10 million (with total unrecovered sums evaluated at roughly Rs. 17.6 million) failed to reach school accounts.

Instead of receiving prompt payments at the end of each season, the school allowed an influential subcommittee, the Rugby Match Organising Committee (RMOC), to hold onto student-earned revenues for over seven years.

When a distinguished alumnus filed a statutory RTI request on 6 February 2024, asking for basic audited statements, interest calculations, and official Ministry correspondence, both Royal College and the Education Ministry met the request with complete radio silence.

Faced with an appeal before the RTIC, Royal College deployed a high-powered legal defence, claiming that the Royal College Union (RCU) is an independent, private alumni body outside school governance, making its accounts confidential. School officials went so far as to argue that the Principal’s position as President of the Union was “purely ceremonial.”

The Commission completely dismantled this narrative:

● The Principal is no bystander: The RTIC pointed out that under the Union’s own constitution and Ministry Circular 54/2023, the Principal presides directly over the Finance Committee, holding active veto and approval power over all financial dealings.

● Public land, public money: The Commission ruled that when an alumni group uses State school facilities to monetise student athletics, it functions as an arm of the public authority. It cannot collect public money and then claim “private immunity.”

● Public interest overrides secrecy: Rebutting arguments that pending Court cases against a former official protected the files, the Commission declared under Section 5(4) that exposing potential financial mismanagement of public funds completely overrides generic confidentiality claims.

The RTIC has given Royal College a strict 30-day ultimatum to surrender certified copies of all income, expenditure, and audit files free of charge.

In an extraordinary warning, the Commission noted that any failure or refusal to comply will trigger immediate criminal prosecution of both the Information Officer and the Public Authority under Section 39 of the RTI Act in the Colombo Magistrate’s Court.

According to observers, this decision sends shockwaves far beyond Reid Avenue. For decades, Big Matches, rugby tournaments, and carnival fundraisers at premier schools across the country have operated through un-audited alumni subcommittees handling hundreds of millions of rupees in cash, ticket sales, and corporate sponsorships.

The Ministry of Education itself admitted during proceedings that it “does not routinely audit” past pupils’ association accounts. The RTIC’s ruling effectively closes this massive regulatory loophole.

“The message from the Commission is clear: alumni clout ends where public accountability begins. School sports revenues belong to the institution and its students, not to unaccountable committees operating behind closed doors,” observers opined.

title: CBSL dollar buying slows to  $ 64 m in September as rupee slips | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 05:51
-     - 182

The Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) was a net buyer of $ 64.2 million from the domestic foreign exchange market in September, down 89% from the record $ 579 million it bought in August, as the rupee weakened against the US dollar after two months of recovery, CBSL data released last Friday showed.

The rupee closed at Rs. 330.83 per dollar on 30 September from Rs. 328.01 at end-August, a depreciation of 0.85% during the month. This widened its year-to-date (YTD) depreciation to 6.3% from 5.5% at end-August, already exceeding the 5.6% decline for the whole of 2025. The rupee had appreciated 10.7% in 2024.

The CBSL purchased $ 85 million in September while selling $ 20.8 million, having recorded no sales in August. September’s net purchases were also 66% lower than the $ 187.8 million bought in September 2025, when the CBSL made no sales.

The September figure was the smallest monthly net purchase since the CBSL resumed buying in June with $ 70.5 million, after being a net seller of $ 12.9 million in April and $ 211.3 million in May. The rupee came under its heaviest pressure in that period following the escalation of the conflict in the Middle East in late February, with its YTD depreciation peaking at 7.9% at end-June.

Purchases then accelerated to $ 348.6 million in July and the record $ 579 million in August, the highest single-month purchase since January 2025, as the rupee recovered, with its YTD depreciation easing to 7.8% by end-July and 5.5% by end-August.

September’s buying took net purchases for the first nine months of 2026 to over $ 1.54 billion, against $ 2 billion for the whole of 2025.

title: Millennium Housing says Athurugiriya land eyed for Metro Bus station entered without consent | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 05:48
-     - 124

Millennium Housing Developers PLC said on Friday its wholly owned subsidiary Millennium Housing Ltd., (MHL) had not consented to the use of its land in Athurugiriya for a proposed Metro Bus Service Station after an unauthorised entry onto the property in which portions of the boundary fencing and gates were removed.

The company said it had received correspondence from the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka (BOI) dated 20 August and 21 September regarding a request made in connection with the proposed bus station on the property, located at No. 23, Kaduwela Road, Oruwala, Athurugiriya.

The company said it had not consented to the release, occupation, acquisition, or use of the property for the project. MHL has retained the land as an asset, earmarked for a future development project in line with the company’s business plans.

On 27 September, the company became aware of an unauthorised entry onto the property and the removal of portions of the boundary fencing and gates, allegedly in connection with the proposed bus station. The company said it had not authorised anyone to enter the property, remove its boundary structures, or begin any work on the land.

The company has lodged an initial complaint with the Athurugiriya Police and is taking legal and administrative steps to protect its and MHL’s rights to the property. It said MHL remains the lawful owner of the land and has not transferred, surrendered, or otherwise consented to its release or occupation.

The company said that any proposed acquisition, occupation, or use of privately owned land must be undertaken through the appropriate legal and statutory process, while respecting the company’s proprietary rights and the interests of its shareholders. It is obtaining legal advice and engaging with the relevant authorities.

The Government launched an expanded Metro Bus Service on 29 September, with 104 new buses operating on seven routes centred on Colombo, aimed at easing traffic congestion and offering a more comfortable, safer public transport service. 

The service, run by Lanka Metro Transit (LMT), added five routes to the two already in operation, and was launched under the patronage of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake. The routes include CM02, linking Millennium City with Colombo Fort, and CM05, linking Battaramulla and Ekala. LMT, introduced in April 2026 under the ‘Clean Sri Lanka’ program, operates as a subsidiary of the Sri Lanka Transport Board, and officials have announced plans to extend the service to Jaffna, Kandy, and Galle.

title: Foreigners back Treasuries, exit CSE as rupee slips 6.3% by end-Aug. | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 05:48
-     - 117

Foreign investors added to their holdings of Government securities in August while continuing to pull money out of the Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE), the Central Bank of Sri Lanka’s (CBSL) External Sector Bulletin for August 2026 showed. Over the same period, the rupee’s depreciation against the US dollar reached 6.3% for the year by end-September.

Foreign investment in the Government securities market recorded a net inflow of $ 70.2 million in August. That took net inflows for the first eight months of the year to $ 208 million, against $ 248 million for the whole of 2025.

The CSE, including both primary and secondary market transactions, recorded a net foreign outflow of $ 58.1 million in August. Net outflows for January to August reached $ 166 million, already exceeding the $ 122 million recorded for the whole of 2025. The market had drawn a net foreign inflow of $ 33 million in 2024.

Taken together, net foreign portfolio flows into Government securities and equities amounted to about $ 42 million in the first eight months of the year.

Foreign direct investment (FDI) reached $ 405 million in the first half of 2026. FDI for the whole of 2025 was $ 1.04 billion, the highest annual figure since 2018, when inflows peaked at $ 1.61 billion. The figures exclude foreign loans from unrelated parties to Board of Investment (BOI) companies.

The rupee closed at Rs. 330.83 per US dollar on 30 September, from Rs. 328.01 at end-August. This took its depreciation against the dollar to 6.3% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis, after a 5.6% decline in 2025 and a 10.7% appreciation in 2024.

The rupee also weakened against other major currencies during the year: by 10.1% against the Chinese yuan, 9.9% against the Australian dollar, 6.3% against the Japanese yen, 4.6% against the pound sterling, and 3% against the euro. It appreciated marginally, by 0.2%, against the Indian rupee.

The current account recorded a deficit of $ 290.6 million in January to August 2026, against a surplus of $ 2.05 billion a year earlier. In August alone, it posted a surplus of $ 133.4 million, down 64.5% from $ 375.9 million.

The merchandise trade deficit widened to $ 7.18 billion in the eight months from $ 4.26 billion. Imports rose 24.1% to $ 16.56 billion, including a 61.6% increase in fuel imports to $ 4.07 billion, while exports rose 3.3% to $ 9.38 billion.

Workers’ remittances rose 19.8% to $ 6.13 billion, though the CBSL noted they may include other remittances, such as those received following Cyclone Ditwah. Net services receipts fell 21.4% to $ 2.1 billion.

Gross official reserves, including the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) swap facility, rose to $ 6.9 billion by end-August from $ 6.8 billion at end-2025, supported by foreign exchange purchases by the CBSL. Reserves were sufficient to cover 3.3 months of imports, down from 3.8 months at end-2025.

title: Lanka Walltiles plans Rs. 5 b Rights Issue to trim debt, to absorb plantation management arm | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 05:47
-     - 95

Lanka Walltiles PLC (LWL) said it is planning to raise Rs. 5 billion through a Rights Issue to partially settle its bank borrowings and overdue intercompany payables, and will amalgamate its wholly owned subsidiary Vallibel Plantation Management Ltd., with itself once the issue is completed.

The Board, at a meeting on 1 October, resolved to recommend the issue of 128,470,588 new ordinary voting shares at Rs. 39 each, in the ratio of eight new shares for every 17 held.

The issue will raise Rs. 5.01 billion and increase the number of shares in issue to 401,470,588 from 273 million, with the new shares making up 32% of the enlarged share base.

The amount compares with LWL’s current stated capital of Rs. 787.77 million, the total capital contributed by shareholders to date.

LWL closed Rs. 0.20 up on Friday at Rs. 43. The share reported net assets of Rs. 83 a share as of end-June 2026. Royal Ceramics Lanka PLC was the top shareholder with a 54.55% stake, followed by A.A. Page’s 7.19%. Royal Ceramics is controlled by Vallibel One PLC, which held a 55.96% stake as at end-June 2026.

The funds will be used to partially settle the company’s existing bank borrowings and overdue intercompany trade and other payables, all of which are interest-bearing. The company said this would substantially strengthen its overall financial position and capital structure.

The Rights Issue is subject to the Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) approving in principle the listing of the new shares and to shareholder approval at an Extraordinary General Meeting, the date of which is yet to be decided.

The Board further resolved that Vallibel Plantation Management will be amalgamated with LWL immediately after the Rights Issue is completed, with LWL continuing as the amalgamated company. The amalgamation is subject to LWL satisfying the solvency test immediately after it takes effect, a statutory requirement that a company be able to pay its debts as they fall due and that its assets exceed its liabilities.

title: Gnanasara Thera remanded, to face Court of Appeal today | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 05:45
-     - 96

Ven. Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera

Bodu Bala Sena (BBS) General Secretary Ven. Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera was arrested on Saturday on an outstanding warrant and remanded until today (5) by the Colombo Magistrate’s Court.

Officers of the Colombo Crime Division (CCD) produced Gnanasara Thera before the Magistrate’s Court yesterday. The court also ordered that steps be taken to produce him before the Court of Appeal today.

The CCD arrested Gnanasara Thera at a forest monastery in Thiniyawala, Kalutara. 

The Court of Appeal had issued a warrant for his arrest on 29 September after he failed to appear before Court in contempt of court proceedings. The Court ordered that he be arrested and produced on 1 October, and directed that the warrant be executed through the Inspector General of Police (IGP).

A two-judge bench comprising Court of Appeal Justices Mayadunne Corea and Lakmali Karunanayake delivered the order on a request by the Attorney General.

The Attorney General had filed a motion seeking the Court’s directions to give effect to a Supreme Court judgement annulling the presidential pardon granted to Gnanasara Thera by former President Maithripala Sirisena.

Gnanasara Thera was not present in Court on 29 September, but was represented by his lawyer.

title: Four-member legal team heads to Saudi Arabia to appeal Anojan death sentence | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 05:42
-     - 47

Anojan Sivarasa

A four-member Sri Lankan legal delegation will leave for Saudi Arabia tomorrow (6) to pursue an appeal against the death sentence imposed on Sri Lankan migrant worker Anojan Sivarasa.

The delegation comprises Attorney General’s Department Additional Solicitor General Azard Navavi, PC, President’s Counsels Faiszer Musthapha and Upul Kumarapperuma, and Attorney-at-Law Hafeel Farisz.

The team will meet representatives of two Saudi law firms retained by the Foreign Ministry to handle the case, and discuss the appeal before the Saudi Supreme Court, at meetings scheduled for 7 and 8 October. The delegation will also finalise the documents for the appeal and meet Saudi officials, Navavi said. The appeal is expected to be filed through the Attorney General’s Department within the stipulated period.

Sivarasa, from Natpittimunai, Kalmunai, was initially sentenced by the Al-Ahsa Criminal Court to five years in prison and fined SR 3 million over a social media statement. His lawyers appealed for a reduced sentence, while Saudi prosecutors separately appealed for a harsher one. The appellate court increased the sentence to death.

The Government is pursuing both legal and diplomatic avenues. President Anura Kumara Dissanayake is expected to send a clemency appeal to the King of Saudi Arabia, to be carried by a separate parliamentary delegation. The Sri Lankan Embassy in Riyadh is monitoring the case and coordinating with Saudi authorities.

The Chief Prelates of the Ramanya Maha Nikaya and the Amarapura Maha Nikaya recently handed the President a memorandum calling for State intervention to secure Sivarasa’s release.

title: Embassy of Korea in Sri Lanka celebrates Korea’s National Foundation Day; 49 years of bilateral ties | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 05:40
-     - 32

Labour Minister and Finance and Planning Deputy Minister Dr. Anil Jayantha Fernando

The Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Sri Lanka on Friday hosted a grand celebration at Shangri-La, Colombo to mark Korea’s 4,359th National Foundation Day. 

This year’s celebration also commemorated 49 years of diplomatic relations between Korea and Sri Lanka, highlighting the longstanding and multifaceted partnership between the two countries.

The occasion was graced by several distinguished guests, including Labour Minister and Finance and Planning Deputy Minister Dr. Anil Jayantha Fernando, who attended as the Chief Guest, Cabinet Ministers, Ministry Secretaries, Ambassadors, members of the Korean community, and representatives from various sectors of Sri Lankan society, all of whom have contributed to the ongoing partnership between Korea and Sri Lanka.

In her opening remarks, Embassy of the Republic of Korea Chargé d’ Affaires Eunji Kang warmly welcomed the guests and highlighted the longstanding and close diplomatic ties between Korea and Sri Lanka, which dates back to 1977.

Emphasising that the bilateral relationship extends far beyond government-to-government cooperation, Kang outlined how Korea-Sri Lanka relations have continued to flourish through strong people-to-people connections in areas such as employment, education, and tourism. She also expressed her appreciation to the Government of Sri Lanka for the introduction of the tourism Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) exemption for Korean nationals, noting that the initiative would help facilitate greater travel and people-to-people exchanges between the two countries.

Commending Sri Lanka’s economic recovery despite a series of internal and external challenges, Kang reaffirmed Korea’s steadfast support for Sri Lanka’s development priorities through close continued cooperation.

In his keynote address, Dr. Fernando, speaking on behalf of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, the Government, and the people of Sri Lanka, extended warm felicitations and heartfelt good wishes to the President, Government, and people of the Republic of Korea on the occasion of Korea’s National Foundation Day.

Referring to the deep-rooted historical ties between Korea and Sri Lanka, dating back to the 5th century AD, Dr. Fernando highlighted the strong people-to-people bonds between the two nations and expressed appreciation for Korea’s steadfast commitment to the welfare and well-being of Sri Lankan workers in Korea.

The Minister also welcomed Korea’s decision to ease its travel advisory for Sri Lanka to Level 1 in 2024, noting the resulting growth in South Korean tourist arrivals, which reached approximately 12,000 in 2025. He further welcomed Korean visitors under Sri Lanka’s visa-free entry scheme.

Recalling with deep gratitude Korea’s solidarity and emergency assistance to Sri Lanka following Cyclone Ditwah, the Minister emphasised Korea’s important role as a longstanding economic partner while highlighting the Government’s keen interest in unlocking further untapped potential, exploring new avenues for business cooperation, and strengthening bilateral trade and investment between the two countries.

This year’s National Foundation Day celebration offered guests a unique sensory experience, showcasing the richness of Korean traditional culture, wellness, technology, and culinary heritage. Reflecting the theme of the ‘K-Initiative,’ the event featured a special showcase of K-beauty products, with the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) presenting a range of Korean cosmetics and skincare products. The showcase demonstrated Korea’s growing global influence in the beauty and wellness industries.

Visitors also had the opportunity to explore the latest technological innovations at a booth hosted by LG Electronics. The display offered a glimpse into Korea’s cutting-edge technological advancements and further highlighted the country’s reputation for innovation.

The Korea Food Corner provided guests with an authentic taste of Korean cuisine, featuring a variety of popular dishes, including Kimbap, Bulgogi, Korean braised chicken, Korean pancakes, Kimchi, and Tteokbokki in three different flavours. Traditional Korean beverages and sweets, including sujeonggwa, yanggaeng, and hangwa, were also served and proved popular among the guests.

As in previous years, the celebration was further enriched by the enthusiastic participation of the Korean community in Sri Lanka. Musical performances by the Sri Lanka Navy Band added to the festive atmosphere, while students from the University of Kelaniya captivated the audience with a performance of ‘Buchaechum,’ the renowned traditional Korean fan dance.

The celebration served not only as a commemoration of Korea’s National Foundation Day but also as a vibrant reflection of the deepening friendship, cultural exchange, and multifaceted cooperation between Korea and Sri Lanka as the two countries approach the 50th anniversary of their diplomatic relations.

title: SL’s Voice of Migrants, Maldives trade  union deepen worker protection cooperation | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 05:38
-     - 20

A new cooperation framework between Sri Lanka’s Voice of Migrants (VOM) and the Maldivian Trade Union Congress (MTUC) is seeking to strengthen protection, information access, and grievance support for Sri Lankan migrant workers in the Maldives.

The two organisations signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on 1 August, establishing a platform for cooperation on issues affecting migrant workers and prospective migrants.

VOM said it has briefed its members on the arrangement and is encouraging them to raise awareness among families of Sri Lankans currently working in the Maldives and among prospective migrants through migrant societies and community networks.

A key component of the initiative is improving access to reliable information before and during migration. The MTUC has agreed to provide VOM with information and awareness materials covering its support services, procedures for seeking assistance, and rules that migrant workers should understand.

VOM said it will explore opportunities to link the initiative with Sri Lanka’s Ministry of Foreign Employment and the Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment (SLBFE), with the objective of extending the benefits of the arrangement to a wider group of existing and prospective migrant workers.

The cooperation is already producing a practical intervention. The MTUC has begun supporting a Sri Lankan migrant worker in the Maldives in connection with the non-implementation of a civil court order relating to compensation, VOM said.

The initiative comes against the backdrop of the importance of overseas employment to Sri Lanka’s economy, with migrant workers contributing significantly to household incomes and the country’s foreign exchange earnings.

VOM said stronger links between migrant organisations, trade unions, and Government agencies could help workers obtain accurate information before departure, understand their rights, and access assistance when disputes arise.

The organisations expect the cooperation to create a more structured support channel for Sri Lankan migrants in the Maldives, while also strengthening awareness among prospective migrants about the procedures, responsibilities, and protections associated with overseas employment.

title: University of Jaffna  Convocation kicks off tomorrow | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 05:38
-     - 21

By Arulkumaran Mahalingam

The 41st General Convocation of the University of Jaffna will be held from 6 to 8 October, with the ceremonies taking place over three days and nine sessions at the University Indoor Stadium.

The Convocation will be presided over by University of Jaffna Chancellor Emeritus Professor Rajaratnam Kumaravadivel, who will confer degrees, postgraduate degrees, diplomas, certificates, Gold medals, prizes, and scholarships on the graduates.

Graduates from 14 faculties will receive their awards at the Convocation. These include the Faculty of Graduate Studies, Faculty of Arts, Faculty of Science, Faculty of Agriculture, Faculty of Management Studies and Commerce, Faculty of Technology, Faculty of Engineering, Faculty of Medicine, Faculty of Hindu Studies, Faculty of Siddha Medicine, Sir Ponnambalam Ramanathan Faculty of Visual and Performing Arts, and the Faculties of Business Studies, Applied Science and Technological Studies of the former Vavuniya Campus of the University of Jaffna.

Graduates who have completed degree programs through the Centre for Open and Distance Learning of the University of Jaffna will also receive their degrees and certificates.

A total of 3,411 degrees will be awarded during the convocation, comprising 314 postgraduate degrees and diplomas, 2,680 degrees to internal students and 417 degrees to external students. In addition, 10 higher diplomas and diplomas, 24 certificates in Professional English, and one qualification certificate in Business Management will be awarded.

A total of 100 Gold medals, 63 prizes, and 15 scholarships will be awarded in recognition of academic achievement across the various degree programs. The University will also confer the prestigious Professor Alagiah Durairajah Gold Medals, awarded annually to outstanding students.

As part of the events associated with the Convocation, a post-Convocation cultural program will be held at the University’s Kailasapathy Auditorium on 10 October from 3 p.m.

Two distinguished memorial lectures will also be held at the Kailasapathy Auditorium on 15 October. The Sir Ponnambalam Ramanathan Memorial Lecture will be delivered at 3 p.m. by University of Jaffna Department of Art History Chair Professor T. Sanathanan. The Lady Leelawathi Ramanathan Memorial Lecture will follow at 4 p.m. and will be delivered by University of Jaffna Department of Sociology Senior Lecturer Dr. I.S. Bakeerathy.

title: Driving licence backlog hits 678,000 as Parliament panel orders probe into DMT delays | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 05:37

About 678,000 driving licences are awaiting printing at the Department of Motor Traffic (DMT), and the backlog continues to grow as daily printing capacity stands at only about 4,600 licences, officials told a Parliamentary committee.

The Sectoral Oversight Committee on Infrastructure and Strategic Development, chaired by MP S.M. Marikkar, instructed officials to conduct a formal investigation into the delays in issuing number plates and driving licences and to submit a full report within 45 days. The report is to cover how the delays began, the administrative and technical factors behind them, and the related tender and procurement process.

Officials said two new printing machines are expected to be installed by 15 October, raising daily capacity to 8,200 licences.

On number plates, officials said plates are now being issued within 14 days for vehicles registered after 10 March.

The Committee stressed the need to upgrade equipment and technical facilities and to put in place a systematic plan to prevent such delays in future. It also inquired into the Department’s administrative efficiency, vacancies, the expediting of procurement, and the prevention of unnecessary delays in public service delivery.

title: Education reforms to extend to Grades 2 and 6 in 2027 | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 05:37
-     - 17

The Cabinet has approved extending the education reforms to Grades 2 and 6 in 2027, while continuing those introduced for Grade 1 this year, Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said last week.

Addressing the weekly post-Cabinet meeting media briefing, Dr. Jayatissa said the approval was based on a concept paper prepared by the National Education Commission (NEC), the National Curriculum Framework, and the School-Based Evaluation and Assessment Guidelines.

The NEC revised the concept paper to incorporate policy recommendations. It will be reviewed by the National Steering Committee for New Education Reforms and its five subcommittees: curriculum reform, human resource development, education administration and infrastructure, evaluation and assessment, and public awareness.

The National Institute of Education (NIE) revised its 2023 National Curriculum Framework in line with the recommendations, and the Steering Committee approved it on 13 August, following approval by the NIE Academic Affairs Board and Institutional Council.

Activity books and teacher guides for all three terms are being prepared for Grades 1 and 2, along with modules and teacher guides for Grade 6. The NIE has trained master trainers for primary and secondary subjects, and provincial teacher training plans are being drawn up.

The Steering Committee has also approved a Policy Guide on School-Based Evaluation and Assessment, prepared by its Evaluation and Assessment SubCommittee, which takes into account the resources available within the school system.
